issue.title: SQL pool timeout

repository.name: stalwart
repository.description: All-in-one Mail & Collaboration server. Secure, scalable and fluent in every protocol (IMAP, JMAP, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV, WebDAV).

issue.body:
I set up a MySQL server as a directory and when starting the mail server everything works for about 5 minutes, after that I get the following error message:
```
pool timed out while waiting for an open connection
```
Here is my pool config:
```toml
[directory."sql".pool]
max-connections = 10
min-connections = 0
```

When I set max-connections to something like 100 it takes about 30 minutes for the error to show up so I'm thinking it might have something to do with connections silently failing until all connections in the pool have failed.

issue.title: `fetch_many` behave differently with MySQL and Postgres

repository.name: sqlx
repository.description: 🧰 The Rust SQL Toolkit. An async, pure Rust SQL crate featuring compile-time checked queries without a DSL. Supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite.

body:
Same issue is reproduced on older version of sqlx. @mdecimus Workaround with `fetch().try_next()` does not help. I also replaced all usages of `fetch_all()` with `fetch().try_collect()` as seen [here](https://github.com/stalwartlabs/mail-server/commit/9725aa75f2f05061b493064b342f2b4eecfbaaee), no luck as well.

I had to tune DB instance `wait_timeout` to 60 seconds, so it automatically drops the inactive connections, I consider this as a dirty workaround.

Unfortunately I cannot provide a minimal working example since it is a big web application using Rocket and `sqlx` via `rocket_db_pools` and I'm not sure which queries are actually eat-up connections.

**Info**

- SQLx version: 0.6.3
- SQLx features enabled: ["macros", "offline", "migrate", "decimal", "chrono", "json"]
- Database server and version: AWS Aurora MySQL "5.7.mysql_aurora.2.11.2"
- Operating system: Amazon Linux 2 (in ECS)
- rustc --version: rustc 1.70.0 (90c541806 2023-05-31)

I came here because I have a very similar issue with my production system.
I did not have the issue in development, the most important difference is probably the version of the systems:
Development: 10.6.12-MariaDB-0ubuntu0.22.04.1 Ubuntu 22.04
Production: 10.11.4-MariaDB-1 Debian 12
SQLx was used by me indirectly through sea-orm, which upgraded SQLx to 0.7 in the last release.
For the time being I will probably downgrade to the previous version. (After the downgrade everything worked as expected again)
